2. Short facts, necessary for disposal of the rule, are that, the respondent No.2-Bank has filed the Artha Rin Suit No.92 of 2006 against the petitioner before the Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka for recovery of realization of Tk.57,71,962/-. Ultimately, the suit was transmitted to the Artha Rin Adalat, Court No.3, Dhaka for disposal and the same was renumbered as Artha Rin Suit No.111 of 2007 and the suit was decreed on 28.10.2009. Thereafter, the respondent No.2-Bank as judgment holder filed Artha Jari Case No.65 of 2010 before the Artha Rin Adalat, Court No.3, Dhaka against the judgment-debtor. During pendency of the same the respondent No.2-Bank filed an application under section 34(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain for issuing warrant of arrest against the petitioner. Having considered the same the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Court No.3, Dhaka by the order dated 20.09.2011 issued warrant of arrest against the petitioner. Challenging the aforesaid order the petitioner moved this writ petition and obtained present Rule. 

 As it appears that Section 34(1) of the Ain provides the civil imprisonment which may be passed on an application filed by the decree-holder. On the other hand sub-Section (9) of Section 34 provides at least a single auction of mortgaged property shall have to be held before passing order of warrant of arrest Mr. Fahad Mohmood Khan for the respondent, however, wanted to impress upon us when the mortgaged property does not exist then how there can be an auction of that property as required under law. But we could not find from the record of Artha Jari Case that any attempt was made for auction sale under Ain, 2003 though the respondent-bank produced a list of moveable property of the judgment-debtor as evident from Annexure-E to the writ petition.
